Apprehending their arrest, petitioners above-named have moved this Court for
grant of anticipatory bail in connection with B. S. City Mahila P.S. Case No.59 of 2020 registered
under Sections 341, 323, 379, 452, 307, 120B/ 34 of the Indian Penal Code.
Heard the parties.

It is submitted by learned counsel for the petitioners that the present case is counter-blast to the earlier cases i.e. Mahila P.S. Case No.14 of 2020, 16 of 2020 and 17 of 2020 registered under different Sections including Sections 498A, 323, 354, 504/34 of the Indian Penal Code and Sections 3 /4 of the D. P. Act.

entities.text: Mahila P.S. Case No.14 of 2020, 16 of 2020 and 17 of 2020
entities.label: CASE_NUMBER

sentences.text: The informant of the present case is one Anita Mishra who happens to be mother-in-law against whom and ors these cases had been registered by their daughter-in-laws.

It is further submitted that offence under Section 307 IPC will not be made out in the present case considering that the informant was all alone at her house when the petitioners/accused barged into the house and allegedly tied the informant.
Intention to cause death is the sine qua non for charge u/s 307.
Had they any such intention, they heavily outnumbered the old lady and there was nothing to prevent them to have caused her death.
There was no serious injury to substantiate the allegation.

The incidence is alleged to have taken place on 25.12.2020 and as per the case of prosecution, it was the Police who had come and rescued the informant, but the case has been registered on 28.12.2020.

sentences.text: Learned APP for the State assisted by learned counsel for the informant have vehemently opposed the prayer.
It is submitted that the victim had sustained head injury on her occipital region which was however to be simple in nature.

It is submitted that immediately after the incidence, station diary entry was made and the victim was sent for treatment to Bokaro General Hospital and,
therefore, the case was registered not on the same day.
In the case filed against the informant under Section 498A IPC, the Police after investigation the informant of this case (Anita Mishra) has not been sent up for trial.
The lady was rescued by the neighbours and that she was tied and kept in a sack and the same has been duly corroborated by the injury report which makes the specific reference.
Considering the submissions of learned counsel and the fact as discussed above, the anticipatory bail application is allowed.

Hence, in the event of their arrest or surrender within a period of three weeks from the date of receipt of a copy of this order before the learned court below, the petitioners named above shall be released on bail on furnishing bail bond of Rs.25,000/- (Rupees Twenty Five Thousand) each with two sureties of the like amount each to the satisfaction of learned Court below,
subject to the conditions laid down under Section 438(2) Cr. P.C.

The petitioners will co-operate in the investigation and will appear on notice under Section 41 A of Cr.P.C. and comply with the condition as laid down under Section 438(2) of the Cr.P.C.
(Gautam Kumar Choudhary, J.) Sandeep/
